name: integer-rating
title: Integer star rating
summary: A five-star rating driven by an exported integer: each star's filled/empty face is chosen by an integer-expression visibility (clamp(0, 1, @rating - k)), a Poor/Okay/Great label by integer division and abs, and a tap cycles 1→5 with valueIntegerExpressionChange (@rating % 5 + 1).
prompt: A five-star rating bound to an integer the host can set; show filled stars up to the rating, a Poor/Okay/Great word, and let a tap on the stars cycle the rating from 1 to 5.
teaches: Write an integer expression wherever an int id is expected (visibility, valueIntegerExpressionChange): a string with an @variable and an operator, e.g. "clamp(0, 1, @rating - 2)", compiles to an IntegerExpression
Show the k-th filled star with visibility clamp(0, 1, @rating - k) (1 = VISIBLE, 0 = GONE) and its empty twin with 1 - clamp(0, 1, @rating - k), stacked in one box
Use integer division as a threshold: @rating / 4 is 1 only for 4 and 5; 1 - min(1, abs(@rating - 3)) is 1 only at exactly 3
Cycle a value on tap with {"type": "valueIntegerExpressionChange", "target": "@rating", "value": "@rating % 5 + 1"}
pitfalls: The integer infix knows only + - * / % (and unary minus) and abs, min, max, clamp; no bit operators, no float functions. / truncates toward zero
A string becomes an integer expression only when it contains an @reference AND one of + - * / %: "clamp(0, 1, @rating)" alone is not one; write "@rating - 0" or reference the variable directly
visibility values are 0 GONE, 1 VISIBLE, 2 INVISIBLE: an expression that can reach 2 hides without collapsing, so clamp it to 0..1
clamp takes (min, max, value) here too
Visibility changes animate (about 300 ms) in the players: capture a tap's result after the transition
The audit reports the tap's IntegerExpression as dead_code: the inspector doesn't count a ValueIntegerExpressionChange action as its reader (a false positive)

Five fixed 44 dp stars need 220 dp: in a narrower host a plain row squeezes the last ones to 0 wide. Give each star box weight 1 with widthIn [0, 44] and centre the row (horizontalArrangement center), since a weighted row fills its width

check.describe: Four yellow stars and one dark, "Great". rating 1 and 3 show one star "Poor" and three stars "Okay"; a tap on the stars goes 4 → 5, a second tap wraps to 1. Resized, the five stars stay centred: at 195 wide they shrink to share the row (weight 1, at most 44 dp each) and a tap on them still goes 4 → 5; at 450 they keep 44 dp.
